title: Build your own
summary: Patch 0020 lets you build. A builder on the toolbar and a kit of 43 snapping pieces - foundations, floors, walls, doors, windows, roofs, stairs, columns, fences and furniture - in four tiers and six empire styles, held up by what's under them and worn down by fire; the towns themselves are now built from the same kit. The game gets its own typeface, Atrapos Sans, and a new flight HUD - a compass bar and round sights that fold in and out. The right-click menu gives way to a free mouse and HUD buttons, the toolbar starts with your tools, ore veins become tendrilled lodes seen as holograms through the ground as you dig, the maps open on you and the worlds orbit their star, you swim and dive, rides and ports are mended, repairs are gone for now, and the automaton is the model you shaped yourself.

steps.title: Building: a kit of snapping pieces
steps.text: Press 5 for the builder and N for its menu: 43 pieces in 9 kinds - square, triangle, half and quarter foundations and floors, walls, half and upper walls, gables, doors, windows with shutters, arches and gates, six roof shapes, straight and spiral stairs, ramps, ladders, each empire's columns, beams, balustrades and fences, and furniture. They snap to each other's edges, corners and tops on a 4 m grid, storeys 3.2 m apart.

diagram.text: BUILDING: A KIT OF SNAPPING PIECES

diagram.label:
snapping to edges,
corners and tops

steps.title: Holding up, tiers and styles
steps.text: A piece needs something holding it up - the preview turns red and says why - and taking a piece away brings down whatever only it held. Timber, stone, marble and bronze reach 1, 2, 2 and 3 cells past a wall or pillar, look their part and cost timber (felled by the digger), Building Stone (cut by every carve), marble and bronze ingots. Six empire styles, eight paints; upgrade a piece in place.

diagram.label:
nothing holding it:
red, and why

taken away: what
it held falls

half back - all of it
in the first minute

steps.title: Building tools
steps.text: Left click places, hold and drag lays a run - a wall's length or a rectangle of floors. K or the middle button turns a piece, O cycles build, demolish, upgrade and paint, P turns snapping off. The preview snaps to the socket nearest your line of sight, skips the taken ones and stays put while the sights wobble; it rides the world every frame, so it never flickers.

steps.title: Doors, furniture, wear
steps.text: Doors, gates, shutters and hatches open with a click; Y locks your own (raiders and predators push the unlocked ones open). Lamps and braziers light the rooms, chests hold 12 stacks, a bed restores you and is where you wake, a workbench and a kiln open the fabricator and the refinery. Fire wears pieces down - soot, then cracks - till they break; a tier up restores them.

diagram.label:
fire wears them:
soot, then cracks

steps.title: Towns from the kit; free building
steps.text: Every town's buildings are now made of the same pieces, in their empire's style - walls, doorways, windows, posts and stairs - merged into blocks drawn only on screen. Structures are saved per world. A sandbox switch (--free-build) makes everything free, needs nothing to hold it up and lets you build in towns.

diagram.text: TOWNS FROM THE KIT; FREE BUILDING

steps.title: Atrapos Sans
steps.text: The game has its own typeface, drawn by a tool from the design sheet and used everywhere - the HUD, the menus, the guide's pictures - with its letters spaced to read easily. Text is never under 12 px: the helpers clamp it, a test checks every screen.

steps.title: The flight HUD
steps.text: Flying has a new HUD: a compass bar along the top with an icon for each kind of thing detected, and round sights in the middle at half the old size - the speed always, the altitude only near a world, the crosshair only when you've locked on a hostile, folding in and out. The ship is drawn over the sights and sits lower; its shots meet in the reticle's middle.

diagram.label:
a compass bar,
an icon a kind

VEL always
ALT near a world

steps.title: Controls and the toolbar
steps.text: The right-click menu is gone: a right click frees the mouse, another captures it. Buttons for the inventory, the maps and the tutorial sit bottom right with their keys over them; M and G open the maps on foot too. No two actions can share a key. The toolbar starts with the rifle, mining beam, digger, scanner and builder; the active slot glows, and the scanner is a tool you fire.

diagram.label:
M, G: the maps
on foot too

steps.title: Veins underground
steps.text: Ore veins are ragged lodes with tendrils now. Scan (Z) and a vein shows as a hologram through the ground - a glass skin under a wireframe cage, never drawn over you - and what you've dug out of it is gone from it as you dig. A fresh hole shows its dug ground at once, never the sky. Excavations are kept through saves.

diagram.label:
Z: a hologram
through the ground

no sky through
a fresh hole

steps.title: Maps, worlds, the sea
steps.text: The maps open on you; the solar map moves smoothly, and the worlds orbit their star in the game. The Automaton has three maps - a 3D planet globe under fog of war with town plans, the solar system and the galaxy. Swim at the surface or dive under: the sea has its own look and life, and the strokes go on as long as you swim.

steps.title: Rides, ports, the automaton
steps.text: A ship you ride never vanishes with you; the local pilot boards and flies his own ship; NPC ramps are solid; the passenger seat is free before the captain sits; ports are lit before you land. Repairs are gone, for other ways to come. The automaton is your own model now - mirrored halves, one shell a bone, crisp corners - layered over the generated one.

review.intro: The code behind patch 0020: the building kit and its tools (scripts/world/build), the towns rebuilt from it, the new typeface (tools/make_font.py), the flight HUD and its compass icons, the controls and toolbar, the veins' hologram and the dug ground, the maps, the sea and swimming, the rides and ports, the repairs removed, and the automaton's overrides - with their tests.

files.explanation: The project notes follow the patch: the Tab menu is now the Automaton, Atrapos Sans and the 12 px minimum join the standing directions, 600 FPS becomes a target rather than a hard floor, and the new character overrides workflow is described with its rules.

-Hits that get through to your hull can damage a [b]part[/b] of your ship - the engines, the sensors, the reactor... - and a damaged part works less well: slower engines, weaker shields, a fuel leak. The log tells you which part was hit.

-[b]Fixing it yourself[/b]
-1. Open the Ship Computer ([b]Tab[/b]) on the [b]Repair[/b] tab, and click the damaged part.
-2. Click the casing's bolts to undo them - opposite ones in turn, never two neighbours, or the casing warps.
-3. Take the [b]Scanner[/b] and sweep the part: rest the lens on what lights up to mark the fault. Each kind of fault shows in its own mode.
-4. Fix each one with its tool: weld cracks slowly, solder burnt wiring (cut the power first!), seal leaks while the pressure's low, tune misaligned parts, and swap wrecked components for spare parts.
-5. Bolt the casing back on.

-Watch the [b]vitals[/b]: too much heat cuts the welder out and undoes half the weld. Nothing you do at the table damages the part - only hits do. hunks.diff:
@@ -1,0 +1,80 @@ # Your work on the characters: overrides
+# Your work on the characters: overrides
+
+The characters (the automaton, the pirate, Kilon, the androids) are **generated**: Blender scripts in
+`external/blender/automaton/` build them, and they're rebuilt whenever they change, so anything done by
+hand in those `.blend` files is lost. **Your** work goes here instead, one file per character, and the
+export layers it over the generated character. You keep your work; the generated base keeps improving
+underneath it.
+
+```
+external/blender/automaton/automaton.blend                     generated - don't edit
+external/blender_overrides/automaton/automaton_overrides.blend  yours
+```
+
+## What's in your file
+
+| Collection / data | What it is |
+|---|---|
+| **Reference** | A copy of the generated character: its rig `Rig`, its parts `gen:Head`, `gen:Torso`, `gen:Arm.L`, `gen:Arm.R`, `gen:Leg.L`, `gen:Leg.R`, `gen:Rifle`, and every clip as an action `gen:walk`, `gen:swim`, ... Look, don't edit: a refresh replaces it. |
+| **Overrides** | Your parts. |
+| Actions without `gen:` | Your clips. |
+
+A generated part you've overridden is hidden in the Reference, so you see yours in its place.
+
+## The rules
+
+- **Parts.** A mesh in *Overrides* named like a generated part (`Head`) **replaces** it. Any other name
+  (`Head_Crest`, `Backpack`) is **added**. Hide a part's render (the camera icon) to leave it out for now.
+- **Rigging.** Parent your part to `Rig`, then either:
+  - skin it: an *Armature* modifier on `Rig` and vertex groups named after bones (`head`; a part spanning
+    bones can have several, e.g. `chest`, `spine`); or
+  - put it on one bone (*Parent > Bone*, e.g. the `head` bone).
+
+  It then follows every animation. Bones: `pelvis spine chest head`, `pauldron/upper/fore/hand/fingers.L/.R`,
+  `thigh/shin/foot.L/.R`, `gun`.
+- **Materials.** Use the existing ones (`AUT_Armor`, `AUT_Armor2`, `AUT_Joint`, `AUT_Red`, `AUT_Red2`,
+  `AUT_Grey`, `AUT_Glow`, `AUT_GlowY`, `AUT_VisorGunmetal`, `AUT_Gun`, `AUT_GunOrange`). The game knows their
+  metal and roughness, the `AUT_Armor`/`AUT_Red`/`AUT_Glow` slots are recolourable, and anything named
+  `AUT_Glow*` glows. A new material works but gets a plain look until the game is taught it (ask).
+- **Joins.** Keep the joins where the generated ones are: the head's neck at about 1.57 m, so there's no
+  gap at the collar. The export warns when your part's bottom sits higher than the generated one's.
+- **Clips.** An action named like a clip (`walk`) **replaces** it; a new name (`wave`) **adds** one (the
+  game plays it once code asks for it). To start from a generated clip, duplicate `gen:walk` and rename
+  the copy `walk`. Custom properties on the action: `loop` (true/false), `gun` (rifle in hand). A clip you
+  replace keeps those from the generated one unless you set them. Names starting `_` are scratch and aren't
+  exported. Animate the `Rig`'s bones, 30 fps.
+- **Modifiers.** Use any (a Mirror on half a part, a Subdivision, a Bevel...): the export applies every modifier
+  except the Armature into the game's copy of your part (your file keeps them live). Put the Mirror (or any
+  shape modifier) above the Armature in the stack. A left part (`Arm.L`, `Leg.L`) with an X Mirror modifier makes
+  the right one too: the generated `Arm.R` is left out (and hidden in the Reference). Give it the right side's
+  vertex groups (`upper.R`...) - the Mirror's *Vertex Groups* option puts the mirrored half on them.
+- **Size.** About the generated part's triangle count (the head: ~1,200) keeps it cheap - after its modifiers.
+
+## The workflow
+
+1. Open `automaton_overrides.blend`. It starts with **your `Head`**: a copy of the generated head, ready to
+   change. Delete it to go back to the generated head.
+2. Model, sculpt or retopo it. Play the Rig's actions (Action editor: `gen:walk` ...) to see it move.
+3. **Export to the game:** Text editor > `export_to_game` > *Run Script* (Alt+P). It saves the file, runs
+   the generated character's export with your overrides merged in (into `art/player_3d/`) and runs Godot's
+   import. The console lists what it took (`OVERRIDE part Head: replaced`) and any problems
+   (`OVERRIDE PROBLEM: ...`). Restart the game to see it.
+4. When the generated character has changed: Text editor > `refresh_reference` > *Run Script*. The
+   Reference is brought up to date; your parts and actions aren't touched.
+
+From a terminal (the project folder):
+
+```
+blender -b external/blender/automaton/automaton.blend --python external/blender/automaton/build.py -- automaton export
+godot --headless --import
+blender -b external/blender_overrides/automaton/automaton_overrides.blend --python external/blender_overrides/overrides.py -- automaton refresh
+blender -b --python external/blender_overrides/overrides.py -- automaton check      # what the export would take, problems
+```
+
+The exported `art/player_3d/model.json` records what was overridden (`"overrides"`), and the game's tests
+fail if it lists a problem.
+
+## Other characters
+
+`blender -b --python external/blender_overrides/overrides.py -- pirate init` makes `pirate/pirate_overrides.blend`
+the same way (any skin with a generated `.blend`: `pirate`, `kilon`, `minoan`, `guard`, ...).

@@ -1,0 +1,444 @@ 
+"""Your own work on the characters, layered over the generated ones.
+
+The generated characters are built by scripts (external/blender/automaton/:
+build.py, kit.py, <skin>.py, moves.py) - rebuilt whenever they change, so
+nothing made by hand in their .blend files lasts. Your work lives here instead,
+one file a character: external/blender_overrides/<skin>/<skin>_overrides.blend.
+
+In it:
+  Reference  - a copy of the generated character: its rig ("Rig"), its parts
+               ("gen:Head", "gen:Torso", "gen:Arm.L" ...) and every clip as an
+               action ("gen:walk", "gen:swim" ...). Refreshed from the
+               generated .blend whenever you like (refresh). Don't edit it: a
+               refresh replaces it.
+  Overrides  - your parts. A mesh named like a generated part ("Head")
+               replaces it; any other name ("Head_Crest") is added. Parent it
+               to "Rig" - skinned (an Armature modifier, vertex groups named
+               after bones: "head") or on a bone (parent type Bone).
+  Actions    - yours, with plain names: "walk" replaces the generated walk,
+               a new name ("wave") adds a clip. (To start from a generated one:
+               duplicate "gen:walk", rename it "walk".) Actions named "_..." are
+               scratch - not exported.
+
+The generated character's export (build.py export) merges all of it in: the
+game gets one model either way, and nothing in the game needs to change.
+
+  blender -b --python overrides.py -- <skin> init      # makes <skin>_overrides.blend (once)
+  blender -b <skin>_overrides.blend --python ../overrides.py -- <skin> refresh   # the Reference brought up to date
+  blender -b --python overrides.py -- <skin> check     # what the export would take, and any problems
+(or, in Blender: the Text editor's "refresh_reference" / "export_to_game" scripts, Run Script.)
+"""
+import os
+import re
+import sys
+
+import bpy
+
+HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
+GEN_DIR = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(HERE), "blender", "automaton")   # (every skin's generated .blend is there)
+PROJECT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(HERE))
+GEN = "gen:"
+REF = "Reference"
+OVR = "Overrides"
+SKIP_OBJECTS = ("KIT_", "SpriteCam")   # (the generated file's lights and camera: not part of the character)
+
+
+def generated_blend(skin):
+    return os.path.join(GEN_DIR, skin + ".blend")
+
+
+def overrides_blend(skin):
+    d = os.environ.get("SA_OVERRIDES_DIR", HERE)   # (a test's own copy, elsewhere)
+    return os.path.join(d, skin, skin + "_overrides.blend")
+
+
+def base(name):
+    """A datablock's name without Blender's ".001" suffix."""
+    return re.sub(r"\.\d{3}$", "", name)
+
+
+def _coll(name, parent=None):
+    c = bpy.data.collections.get(name)
+    if c is None:
+        c = bpy.data.collections.new(name)
+        (parent or bpy.context.scene.collection).children.link(c)
+    return c
+
+
+# --- In your file: the Reference -----------------------------------------------------
+
+def refresh(skin):
+    """The Reference brought up to date from the generated character: its rig's
+    bones, its parts and its clips replaced - your Overrides (parented to "Rig")
+    and your own actions untouched."""
+    path = generated_blend(skin)
+    if not os.path.exists(path):
+        raise SystemExit("no generated character at %s - build it first (build.py %s model / actions)" % (path, skin))
+    ref = _coll(REF)
+    _coll(OVR)
+    old_rig = bpy.data.objects.get("Rig")
+    had_mats = {m.name: m for m in bpy.data.materials}
+    with bpy.data.libraries.load(path, link=False) as (src, dst):
+        dst.objects = [n for n in src.objects if not n.startswith(SKIP_OBJECTS)]
+        dst.actions = list(src.actions)
+    new_objs = [o for o in dst.objects if o is not None]
+    new_rig = next(o for o in new_objs if o.type == "ARMATURE")
+    root = next((o for o in new_objs if o.type == "EMPTY" and base(o.name) == "Root"), None)
+    # The rig: kept as the same object (your parts stay parented to it), its bones the new ones.
+    if old_rig is None:
+        rig = new_rig
+        rig.name = "Rig"
+    else:
+        rig = old_rig
+        old_data = rig.data
+        rig.data = new_rig.data
+        rig.data.name = "Rig"
+        rig.matrix_world = new_rig.matrix_world.copy()
+        bpy.data.objects.remove(new_rig)
+        if old_data.users == 0:
+            bpy.data.armatures.remove(old_data)
+    if root is not None:
+        old_root = bpy.data.objects.get("Root")
+        if old_root is not None and old_root is not root:
+            bpy.data.objects.remove(old_root)
+        root.name = "Root"
+    # The parts: the old reference ones out, the new ones in (named "gen:<part>").
+    for o in list(ref.objects):
+        if o not in (rig, root) and o.type == "MESH":
+            bpy.data.objects.remove(o)
+    for o in new_objs:
+        if o is new_rig or o is root or o is rig:
+            continue
+        if o.type != "MESH":
+            bpy.data.objects.remove(o)
+            continue
+        for c in list(o.users_collection):
+            c.objects.unlink(o)
+        ref.objects.link(o)
+        o.name = GEN + base(o.name)
+        o.parent = rig
+        for m in o.modifiers:
+            if m.type == "ARMATURE":
+                m.object = rig
+        o.hide_select = True   # (a reference: look, don't touch)
+    for o in (rig, root):
+        if o is not None:
+            for c in list(o.users_collection):
+                c.objects.unlink(o)
+            ref.objects.link(o)
+    if root is not None:
+        rig.parent = root
+    # The clips: the old generated actions out, the new ones in as "gen:<clip>" (kept on save).
+    for a in list(bpy.data.actions):
+        if a.name.startswith(GEN) and a not in dst.actions:
+            bpy.data.actions.remove(a)
+    for a in dst.actions:
+        if a is None:
+            continue
+        a.name = GEN + base(a.name)
+        a.use_fake_user = True
+    for a in bpy.data.actions:
+        if not a.name.startswith(GEN):
+            a.use_fake_user = True   # (yours too: an action no rig is playing is otherwise dropped on save)
+    if rig.animation_data is None:
+        rig.animation_data_create()
+    if rig.animation_data.action is None or rig.animation_data.action.name not in bpy.data.actions:
+        idle = bpy.data.actions.get(GEN + "idle")
+        if idle:
+            rig.animation_data.action = idle
+    # The materials: the fresh ones take the old names (your parts using "AUT_Armor" get the new one).
+    for m in list(bpy.data.materials):
+        if m.name in had_mats:
+            continue
+        b = base(m.name)
+        old = had_mats.get(b)
+        if old is not None and b != m.name:
+            old.user_remap(m)
+            bpy.data.materials.remove(old)
+            m.name = b
+    _hide_overridden()
+    for lib in list(bpy.data.libraries):
+        if lib.users == 0:
+            bpy.data.libraries.remove(lib)
+    print("REFRESHED %s: %d parts, %d clips from %s" % (skin, len([o for o in ref.objects if o.type == "MESH"]),
+                                                      len([a for a in bpy.data.actions if a.name.startswith(GEN)]), path))
+
+
+def mirrored_to(o):
+    """A left part ("Arm.L") with an X Mirror modifier: the right one it makes too ("Arm.R"), else ""."""
+    name = base(o.name)
+    if not name.endswith(".L"):
+        return ""
+    for m in o.modifiers:
+        if m.type == "MIRROR" and m.use_axis[0] and m.show_render:
+            return name[:-2] + ".R"
+    return ""
+
+
+def _hide_overridden():
+    """A generated part your Overrides replace: hidden in the Reference (so you see yours in its place) -
+    a mirrored left part's right one too."""
+    mine = {base(o.name) for o in _coll(OVR).all_objects if o.type == "MESH"}
+    mine |= {mirrored_to(o) for o in _coll(OVR).all_objects if o.type == "MESH"} - {""}
+    for o in _coll(REF).objects:
+        if o.name.startswith(GEN):
+            hide = o.name[len(GEN):] in mine
+            o.hide_viewport = hide
+            o.hide_render = hide
+
+
+def init(skin):
+    """A new overrides file for `skin`: the Reference, an empty Overrides
+    collection - and, to start from, a copy of the generated head as your "Head"
+    (the same as the generated one until you change it: delete it to go back)."""
+    path = overrides_blend(skin)
+    if os.path.exists(path):
+        raise SystemExit("%s exists already - refresh it instead" % path)
+    bpy.ops.wm.read_homefile(use_empty=True)
+    bpy.context.scene.name = skin + " overrides"
+    refresh(skin)
+    rig = bpy.data.objects["Rig"]
+    gen_head = bpy.data.objects.get(GEN + "Head")
+    if gen_head is not None:
+        head = gen_head.copy()
+        head.data = gen_head.data.copy()
+        head.name = "Head"
+        head.data.name = "Head"
+        head.hide_select = False
+        head.hide_viewport = False
+        head.hide_render = False
+        for m in list(head.modifiers):
+            if m.type != "ARMATURE":
+                head.modifiers.remove(m)   # (the generated ink shell: not wanted)
+        if "ink" in head.vertex_groups:
+            head.vertex_groups.remove(head.vertex_groups["ink"])
+        ink = head.data.materials.find("KIT_Ink")
+        if ink >= 0:
+            head.data.materials.pop(index=ink)
+        _coll(OVR).objects.link(head)
+        head.parent = rig
+    _hide_overridden()
+    _scripts(skin)
+    # A plain light and a view onto the head, for a start.
+    bpy.context.scene.render.engine = "BLENDER_EEVEE" if "BLENDER_EEVEE" in [e.identifier for e in bpy.types.RenderSettings.bl_rna.properties["engine"].enum_items] else bpy.context.scene.render.engine
+    sun = bpy.data.objects.new("Sun", bpy.data.lights.new("Sun", "SUN"))
+    sun.rotation_euler = (0.8, 0.2, 0.6)
+    bpy.context.scene.collection.objects.link(sun)
+    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(path), exist_ok=True)
+    bpy.ops.wm.save_as_mainfile(filepath=path, relative_remap=True)
+    print("MADE", path)
+
+
+def _scripts(skin):
+    """Two scripts in the file's Text editor: refresh the Reference; export to the game."""
+    refresh_src = '''# Run Script (Alt+P): the Reference brought up to date from the generated %(skin)s.
+import bpy, sys, os
+d = bpy.path.abspath("//..")
+sys.path.insert(0, d)
+import importlib, overrides
+importlib.reload(overrides)
+overrides.refresh("%(skin)s")
+''' % {"skin": skin}
+    export_src = '''# Run Script (Alt+P): this file saved, then the game's %(skin)s exported with your
+# overrides merged in (build.py export) and Godot's import run. Watch the console.
+import bpy, subprocess, os, sys
+bpy.ops.wm.save_mainfile()
+here = bpy.path.abspath("//")
+gen = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(here, "..", "..", "blender", "automaton"))
+project = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(here, "..", "..", ".."))
+r = subprocess.run([bpy.app.binary_path, "-b", os.path.join(gen, "%(skin)s.blend"), "--python",
+                    os.path.join(gen, "build.py"), "--", "%(skin)s", "export"], capture_output=True, text=True)
+out = r.stdout + r.stderr
+print("\\n".join(l for l in out.splitlines() if l.startswith(("EXPORTED", "OVERRIDE", "Error", "Traceback"))) or out[-3000:])
+try:
+    subprocess.run(["godot", "--headless", "--path", project, "--import"], capture_output=True, timeout=600)
+    print("Godot import done: restart the game (or its window) to see it.")
+except Exception as e:
+    print("Godot import not run (%%s): open the project in Godot, or run godot --headless --import" %% e)
+''' % {"skin": skin}
+    for name, src in (("refresh_reference", refresh_src), ("export_to_game", export_src)):
+        t = bpy.data.texts.get(name) or bpy.data.texts.new(name)
+        t.from_string(src)
+
+
+# --- In the export: your work merged in -----------------------------------------------
+
+def apply(skin, arm, coll, log=print):
+    """Called by build.py's export on the generated character (`arm`: its rig,
+    `coll`: its collection): your Overrides' parts and actions brought in -
+    a part with a generated part's name replacing it, others added; an action
+    with a clip's name replacing it, others added. Returns
+    {"parts": {name: "replaced" | "added"}, "clips": {name: "replaced" | "added"}, "problems": [...]}."""
+    out = {"parts": {}, "clips": {}, "problems": []}
+    path = overrides_blend(skin)
+    if not os.path.exists(path):
+        return out
+    bones = {b.name for b in arm.data.bones}
+    with bpy.data.libraries.load(path, link=False) as (src, dst):
+        dst.collections = [OVR] if OVR in src.collections else []
+        dst.actions = [n for n in src.actions if not n.startswith((GEN, "_"))]
+    mine = []
+    if dst.collections and dst.collections[0] is not None:
+        oc = dst.collections[0]
+        mine = [o for o in oc.all_objects if o.type == "MESH" and not o.hide_render]
+    gen_parts = {o.name: o for o in coll.objects if o.type == "MESH" and o.parent == arm}
+    gen_low = {n: min((o.matrix_world @ v.co).z for v in o.data.vertices) for n, o in gen_parts.items() if len(o.data.vertices)}
+    for o in mine:
+        name = base(o.name)
+        twin = mirrored_to(o)   # (a left part mirrored: the generated right one goes too - the mirror makes it)
+        # On the generated rig: parented to it, skinned to it - as yours were to the Reference's "Rig".
+        mw = o.matrix_world.copy()
+        o.parent = arm
+        o.matrix_world = mw
+        for m in o.modifiers:
+            if m.type == "ARMATURE":
+                m.object = arm
+        if o.parent_type == "BONE" and o.parent_bone not in bones:
+            out["problems"].append("%s: on bone %r - the rig has no such bone" % (name, o.parent_bone))
+        groups = [g.name for g in o.vertex_groups if g.name != "ink"]
+        if o.parent_type != "BONE":
+            if not groups:
+                out["problems"].append("%s: no vertex groups - skin it to bones (e.g. a group \"head\" with every vertex)" % name)
+            unknown = [g for g in groups if g not in bones]
+            if unknown:
+                out["problems"].append("%s: vertex groups %s aren't bones of the rig" % (name, unknown))
+            if groups:
+                n = _weigh_strays(o)
+                if n:
+                    out.setdefault("notes", []).append("%s: %d vertices were on no bone (added geometry not assigned to a vertex group) - "
+                                                       "given the bones of the nearest weighted vertex; assign them in Blender to choose" % (name, n))
+        # Its materials: the generated ones where the names match (the game knows those: their look, their recolouring).
+        for i, slot in enumerate(o.material_slots):
+            mat = slot.material
+            if mat is None:
+                continue
+            known = bpy.data.materials.get(base(mat.name))
+            if known is not None and known is not mat and known.library is None and base(mat.name) == known.name:
+                o.material_slots[i].material = known
+            elif not base(mat.name).startswith(("AUT_", "KIT_", "MIN_", "PIR_", "KIL_")):
+                out["problems"].append("%s: material %r is new to the game - it'll get a plain look (name it after a known one, "
+                                       "or ask for it to be taught)" % (name, mat.name))
+        for c in list(o.users_collection):
+            c.objects.unlink(o)
+        coll.objects.link(o)
+        baked = _bake_modifiers(o)   # (in the scene now: its modifiers evaluated)
+        if baked:
+            out.setdefault("notes", []).append("%s: its %s modifier%s applied for the game (the Armature kept)" % (
+                name, ", ".join(baked), "s" if len(baked) > 1 else ""))
+        if name in gen_parts:
+            g = gen_parts.pop(name)
+            low = min((o.matrix_world @ v.co).z for v in o.data.vertices) if len(o.data.vertices) else 0.0
+            if name in gen_low and low > gen_low[name] + 0.03:
+                out["problems"].append("%s: its lowest point is %.0f mm above the generated one's - a gap at the join?" % (
+                    name, (low - gen_low[name]) * 1000.0))
+            bpy.data.objects.remove(g)
+            out["parts"][name] = "replaced"
+        else:
+            out["parts"][name] = "added"
+        if twin and twin in gen_parts:
+            bpy.data.objects.remove(gen_parts.pop(twin))
+            out["parts"][twin] = "mirrored from %s" % name
+        o.name = name
+    # Anything else the parts dragged in (the Reference's rig, its root): not wanted.
+    for o in list(bpy.data.objects):
+        if o is not arm and o not in mine and not o.users_scene:
+            bpy.data.objects.remove(o)
+    if dst.collections and dst.collections[0] is not None:
+        bpy.data.collections.remove(dst.collections[0])
+    for a in dst.actions:
+        if a is None:
+            continue
+        name = base(a.name)
+        old = bpy.data.actions.get(name)
+        if old is not None and old is not a:
+            bpy.data.actions.remove(old)
+            out["clips"][name] = "replaced"
+        else:
+            out["clips"][name] = "added"
+        a.name = name
+    for p in out["problems"]:
+        log("OVERRIDE PROBLEM: " + p)
+    for p in out.get("notes", []):
+        log("OVERRIDE NOTE: " + p)
+    for k, v in out["parts"].items():
+        log("OVERRIDE part %s: %s" % (k, v))
+    for k, v in out["clips"].items():
+        log("OVERRIDE clip %s: %s" % (k, v))
+    return out
+
+
+def _bake_modifiers(o):
+    """Your part's modifiers other than the Armature (a Mirror, a Subdivision, a Bevel...)
+    applied into its mesh for the game (the glTF export leaves modifiers live: a mirrored
+    half would come out half) - its vertex groups kept, so it's still skinned; the Armature
+    modifier stays. Done on the export's own copy, never your file. The modifiers' types."""
+    others = [m for m in o.modifiers if m.type != "ARMATURE"]
+    if not others or o.type != "MESH":
+        return []
+    arms = [m for m in o.modifiers if m.type == "ARMATURE"]
+    was = [m.show_viewport for m in arms]
+    for m in arms:
+        m.show_viewport = False   # (the mesh at rest: the armature deforms it in the game)
+    for m in others:
+        m.show_viewport = True
+    dg = bpy.context.evaluated_depsgraph_get()
+    dg.update()
+    new = bpy.data.meshes.new_from_object(o.evaluated_get(dg), preserve_all_data_layers=True, depsgraph=dg)
+    for m, w in zip(arms, was):
+        m.show_viewport = w
+    types = [m.type.capitalize() for m in others]
+    for m in others:
+        o.modifiers.remove(m)
+    old = o.data
+    o.data = new
+    if old.users == 0:
+        bpy.data.meshes.remove(old)
+    return types
+
+
+def _weigh_strays(o):
+    """A skinned part's vertices on no bone (geometry added in Edit Mode isn't put in a
+    vertex group by itself - the armature then never moves it): each given the bone
+    weights of the nearest vertex that has some. How many there were."""
+    from mathutils import kdtree
+    me = o.data
+    real = {g.index for g in o.vertex_groups if g.name != "ink"}
+    weighted = [v for v in me.vertices if any(g.group in real and g.weight > 0.0 for g in v.groups)]
+    strays = [v for v in me.vertices if not any(g.group in real and g.weight > 0.0 for g in v.groups)]
+    if not strays or not weighted:
+        return 0
+    kd = kdtree.KDTree(len(weighted))
+    for i, v in enumerate(weighted):
+        kd.insert(v.co, i)
+    kd.balance()
+    for v in strays:
+        _, i, _ = kd.find(v.co)
+        for g in weighted[i].groups:
+            if g.group in real and g.weight > 0.0:
+                o.vertex_groups[g.group].add([v.index], g.weight, "REPLACE")
+    return len(strays)
+
+
+def main():
+    argv = sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--") + 1:] if "--" in sys.argv else []
+    if len(argv) < 2:
+        print(__doc__)
+        return
+    skin, cmd = argv[0], argv[1]
+    if cmd == "init":
+        init(skin)
+    elif cmd == "refresh":
+        refresh(skin)
+        bpy.ops.wm.save_mainfile()
+    elif cmd == "check":
+        bpy.ops.wm.open_mainfile(filepath=generated_blend(skin))
+        arm = bpy.data.objects["Rig"]
+        coll = arm.users_collection[0]
+        r = apply(skin, arm, coll)
+        print("CHECK %s: parts %s, clips %s, %d problem(s)" % (skin, r["parts"], r["clips"], len(r["problems"])))
+    else:
+        print(__doc__)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

A left part with an X Mirror modifier also stands for its right twin, so the generated right part is left out.
A new overrides file: the Reference, an empty Overrides collection and a copy of the generated head to start from.

files.explanation: New: the planet map's fog of war. Each world has a 128 x 64 grid of how well each patch of ground has been seen, revealed in soft caps round you as you walk or fly low, and saved compressed in the galaxy's data.

hunks.diff:
@@ -1,0 +1,123 @@ 
+class_name PlanetFog
+extends RefCounted
+## Fog of war on a planet (the planet map's - PlanetMapPage): a coarse grid
+## of how well each patch of its ground has been seen (0 never .. 255 seen),
+## COLS x ROWS cells of longitude and latitude (planet-local directions, north
+## +Y - the HUD's), revealed in soft-edged caps round you as you walk or fly
+## low (CosmosMapMirror: Galaxy.reveal_planet), saved as base64 (deflated:
+## Galaxy "planet_explored"). The globe draws texture() over its ground (dark
+## where you haven't been) and hides what lies in the dark.
+
+const COLS := 128
+const ROWS := 64
+## Seen at least this much: explored (its things show on the map).
+const SEEN := 110
+
+var data := PackedByteArray()
+var _image: Image
+var _texture: ImageTexture
+var _dirty := true
+var version := 0                    # (counts the changes: the map redraws when it moves on)
+
+
+func _init() -> void:
+	data.resize(COLS * ROWS)
+
+
+## The cell of a planet-local direction.
+static func cell_of(d: Vector3) -> Vector2i:
+	var u := d.normalized()
+	var lat := asin(clampf(u.y, -1.0, 1.0))
+	var lon := atan2(u.x, u.z)
+	return Vector2i(clampi(int((lon + PI) / TAU * COLS), 0, COLS - 1), clampi(int((PI * 0.5 - lat) / PI * ROWS), 0, ROWS - 1))
+
+
+## A cell's middle as a direction.
+static func dir_of(x: int, y: int) -> Vector3:
+	var lon := (x + 0.5) / COLS * TAU - PI
+	var lat := PI * 0.5 - (y + 0.5) / ROWS * PI
+	return Vector3(cos(lat) * sin(lon), sin(lat), cos(lat) * cos(lon))
+
+
+## Reveals a cap round `d` (planet-local) `ang` radians wide; true if anything
+## new was seen. Only the rows and columns it can touch are visited.
+func reveal(d: Vector3, ang: float) -> bool:
+	var u := d.normalized()
+	var lat := asin(clampf(u.y, -1.0, 1.0))
+	var ang_c := maxf(ang, PI / ROWS * 0.75)
+	var soft := maxf(ang_c * 0.35, PI / ROWS)
+	var y0 := clampi(int((PI * 0.5 - (lat + ang_c)) / PI * ROWS) - 1, 0, ROWS - 1)
+	var y1 := clampi(int((PI * 0.5 - (lat - ang_c)) / PI * ROWS) + 1, 0, ROWS - 1)
+	var lon := atan2(u.x, u.z)
+	var cl := cos(lat)
+	var full := cl < 0.05 or absf(lat) + ang_c > PI * 0.5 - 0.05
+	var span := 0 if full else mini(COLS >> 1, int(ang_c / maxf(cl * cos(minf(absf(lat) + ang_c, 1.5)), 0.05) / TAU * COLS) + 2)
+	var xc := int((lon + PI) / TAU * COLS)
+	var xs := range(COLS) if full else range(xc - span, xc + span + 1)
+	var changed := false
+	for y in range(y0, y1 + 1):
+		for xk in xs:
+			var x := posmod(xk, COLS)
+			var a := u.angle_to(dir_of(x, y))
+			if a > ang_c:
+				continue
+			var v := int(clampf((ang_c - a) / soft, 0.0, 1.0) * 255.0)
+			var i := y * COLS + x
+			if v > data[i]:
+				data[i] = v
+				changed = true
+	if changed:
+		_dirty = true
+		version += 1
+	return changed
+
+
+func seen_at(d: Vector3) -> int:
+	var c := cell_of(d)
+	return data[c.y * COLS + c.x]
+
+
+func explored(d: Vector3) -> bool:
+	return seen_at(d) >= SEEN
+
+
+## Share of the world explored (0..1).
+func explored_share() -> float:
+	var n := 0
+	for v in data:
+		if v >= SEEN:
+			n += 1
+	return float(n) / data.size()
+
+
+func reveal_all() -> void:
+	data.fill(255)
+	_dirty = true
+	version += 1
+
+
+## The fog as a texture (L8: 0 unseen .. 1 seen), its cells in longitude
+## (x, from -180) and latitude (y, from the north).
+func texture() -> ImageTexture:
+	if _dirty or _texture == null:
+		_image = Image.create_from_data(COLS, ROWS, false, Image.FORMAT_L8, data)
+		if _texture == null:
+			_texture = ImageTexture.create_from_image(_image)
+		else:
+			_texture.update(_image)
+		_dirty = false
+	return _texture
+
+
+func save() -> String:
+	return Marshalls.raw_to_base64(data.compress(FileAccess.COMPRESSION_DEFLATE))
+
+
+func load_from(s: String) -> void:
+	if s == "":
+		return
+	var raw := Marshalls.base64_to_raw(s).decompress(COLS * ROWS, FileAccess.COMPRESSION_DEFLATE)
+	if raw.size() == COLS * ROWS:
+		data = raw
+		_dirty = true
+		version += 1
hunks.title: PlanetFog
hunks.note: One byte a cell over longitude and latitude (8192 cells a planet). The globe draws it as a texture over its ground and hides what's in the dark.

bubbles.text: A cell seen at least this much counts as explored: towns, caves and camps in it show on the map.
A planet-local direction becomes a cell from its longitude (atan2) and latitude (asin), with north as +Y.

bubbles.at: func reveal(d: Vector3, ang: float) -> bool:
bubbles.text: Brightens a round cap of cells by their angle from you, with a soft edge (a cell only ever gets brighter). Only the rows and columns the cap can reach are visited, and near the poles the whole row.
A counter of changes: the map redraws its globe only when this moves on.
The share of cells explored, shown as the % explored on the planet map.
The grid is uploaded as an L8 texture only when it has changed, and the same ImageTexture is updated in place.
Saved as deflate-compressed bytes in base64, so a mostly dark world takes little room in the save.

files.explanation: New: the builder's menu (N with the builder in hand). It lists the kit's pieces by category with their pictures and costs in the chosen tier, and has rows for the tier, the empire style, the paint, the mode and snapping.

@@ -1,0 +1,226 @@ 
+class_name BuildMenu
+extends Control
+## The builder's menu (N with the builder in hand - CosmosBuilds): the pieces
+## by category, each with its picture and what it costs in the chosen tier;
+## the tier (timber, stone, marble, bronze - how far each reaches out from a
+## support, how tough), the empire's style, a paint, the mode (build,
+## demolish, upgrade, paint) and snapping. A piece clicked: in hand, the menu
+## shut.
+
+const CAT_TABS := ["Foundations", "Floors", "Walls", "Openings", "Roofs", "Stairs", "Supports", "Fences", "Furniture"]
+
+var builds: CosmosBuilds
+var _cat := 0
+var _tabs: HBoxContainer
+var _grid: GridContainer
+var _tiers: HBoxContainer
+var _styles: HBoxContainer
+var _paints: HBoxContainer
+var _modes: HBoxContainer
+var _snap: Button
+var _note: Label
+var _have: Label
+var _root: VBoxContainer
+
+
+func _ready() -> void:
+	hide()
+	set_anchors_and_offsets_preset(PRESET_FULL_RECT)
+	Keybinds.register_menu(self)
+
+
+func _build() -> void:
+	_root = UI.modal(self, Color(NeonTheme.TEXT_DIM, 0.9), Vector2(1180, 0))
+	var header := HBoxContainer.new()
+	header.add_child(UI.label("BUILDER", 28, NeonTheme.HEAD))
+	header.add_child(UI.spacer())
+	header.add_child(EditorIcons.dress(UI.button("", close), "close", EditorIcons.tip("Close", "N / Esc", "Back to building.")))
+	_root.add_child(header)
+	_tabs = UI.tab_bar(CAT_TABS, _pick_cat)
+	_root.add_child(_tabs)
+	_grid = GridContainer.new()
+	_grid.columns = 5
+	_grid.add_theme_constant_override("h_separation", 10)
+	_grid.add_theme_constant_override("v_separation", 10)
+	_root.add_child(_grid)
+	_tiers = _row("TIER")
+	for i in BuildKit.TIERS.size():
+		_tiers.add_child(_toggle(BuildKit.tier_name(i), func(): _choose("tier", i)))
+	_styles = _row("STYLE")
+	for s in BuildKit.STYLES:
+		_styles.add_child(_toggle(BuildKit.STYLE_NAMES[s], func(): _choose("style", s)))
+	_paints = _row("PAINT")
+	for i in BuildKit.PAINTS.size():
+		var b := Swatch.new()
+		b.paint = i
+		b.tooltip_text = BuildKit.PAINT_NAMES[i]
+		b.pressed.connect(func(): _choose("paint", i))
+		_paints.add_child(b)
+	_modes = _row("MODE")
+	for m in CosmosBuilds.MODES:
+		_modes.add_child(_toggle(CosmosBuilds.MODE_NAMES[m], func(): _choose("mode", m)))
+	_modes.add_child(UI.spacer())
+	_snap = _toggle("Snapping", func(): _choose("snap", 0))
+	_modes.add_child(_snap)
+	_note = UI.label("", 16, NeonTheme.TEXT)
+	_root.add_child(_note)
+	_have = UI.label("", 16, NeonTheme.TEXT_DIM)
+	_root.add_child(_have)
+
+
+func _row(title: String) -> HBoxContainer:
+	var h := HBoxContainer.new()
+	h.add_theme_constant_override("separation", 8)
+	var l := UI.label(title, 16, NeonTheme.HEAD)
+	l.custom_minimum_size.x = 84
+	h.add_child(l)
+	_root.add_child(h)
+	return h
+
+
+func _toggle(text: String, act: Callable) -> Button:
+	var b := UI.light_button(UI.button(text, act, 16))
+	b.toggle_mode = true
+	b.focus_mode = Control.FOCUS_NONE
+	b.custom_minimum_size = Vector2(118, 38)
+	return b
+
+
+func _choose(what: String, v) -> void:
+	match what:
+		"tier": CosmosBuilds.tier = int(v)
+		"style": CosmosBuilds.style = str(v)
+		"paint": CosmosBuilds.paint = int(v)
+		"mode": CosmosBuilds.mode = str(v)
+		"snap": CosmosBuilds.snap_on = not CosmosBuilds.snap_on
+	refresh()
+
+
+func _pick_cat(i: int) -> void:
+	_cat = i
+	refresh()
+
+
+func open() -> void:
+	if _root == null:
+		_build()
+	var cat := str(BuildKit.info(CosmosBuilds.piece).get("cat", "found"))
+	for i in BuildKit.CATS.size():
+		if BuildKit.CATS[i][0] == cat:
+			_cat = i
+	var was_open := visible and not HexReveal.closing(self)
+	show()
+	refresh()
+	if not was_open:
+		HexReveal.play(self)
+
+
+func close() -> void:
+	if not visible:
+		return
+	HexReveal.play(self, true, hide)
+
+
+func refresh() -> void:
+	UI.select_tab(_tabs, _cat)
+	UI.clear(_grid)
+	for id in BuildKit.ids_in(str(BuildKit.CATS[_cat][0])):
+		var t := Tile.new()
+		t.id = id
+		t.cost = BuildKit.cost_text(BuildKit.cost(id, CosmosBuilds.tier))
+		t.ok = _affordable(BuildKit.cost(id, CosmosBuilds.tier))
+		t.picked = id == CosmosBuilds.piece
+		t.tooltip_text = "%s\n%s" % [BuildKit.title(id, CosmosBuilds.tier), t.cost]
+		t.pressed.connect(func():
+			builds.choose(id)
+			close())
+		_grid.add_child(t)
+	for i in _tiers.get_child_count() - 1:
+		(_tiers.get_child(i + 1) as Button).set_pressed_no_signal(i == CosmosBuilds.tier)
+	for i in BuildKit.STYLES.size():
+		(_styles.get_child(i + 1) as Button).set_pressed_no_signal(BuildKit.STYLES[i] == CosmosBuilds.style)
+	for i in BuildKit.PAINTS.size():
+		var sw := _paints.get_child(i + 1) as Swatch
+		sw.on = i == CosmosBuilds.paint
+		sw.queue_redraw()
+	for i in CosmosBuilds.MODES.size():
+		(_modes.get_child(i + 1) as Button).set_pressed_no_signal(CosmosBuilds.MODES[i] == CosmosBuilds.mode)
+	_snap.set_pressed_no_signal(CosmosBuilds.snap_on)
+	_snap.text = "Snapping on" if CosmosBuilds.snap_on else "Snapping off"
+	var T: Dictionary = BuildKit.TIERS[CosmosBuilds.tier]
+	_note.text = "%s: floors reach %d cell%s past a wall or pillar  ·  %d toughness a wall  ·  %s style" % [T["name"], int(T["span"]) - 1, "" if int(T["span"]) == 2 else "s", BuildKit.hp_of("wall", CosmosBuilds.tier),
+		BuildKit.STYLE_NAMES.get(CosmosBuilds.style, "")]
+	var parts := []
+	for k in ["timber", "stone", "marble", "bronze_ingots"]:
+		parts.append("%d %s" % [CosmosBuilds.have(k), Items.display_name(k)])
+	_have.text = "Free building: no costs, no supports needed" if BuildKit.free_build else "You have " + "  ·  ".join(parts)
+	UI.scale_fonts(_root, "menu", 1.3)
+
+
+static func _affordable(c: Dictionary) -> bool:
+	if BuildKit.free_build:
+		return true
+	for k in c:
+		if CosmosBuilds.have(k) < int(c[k]):
+			return false
+	return true
+
+
+func _input(event: InputEvent) -> void:
+	if not visible or UI.esc_menu_open():
+		return
+	if event.is_action_pressed("ui_cancel") or (event is InputEventKey and Keybinds.pressed(event, "build_menu")):
+		close()
+		get_viewport().set_input_as_handled()
+
+
+## A piece's tile: its picture, its name, what it costs (dim when you can't afford it).
+class Tile:
+	extends Button
+	var id := ""
+	var cost := ""
+	var ok := true
+	var picked := false
+
+	func _init() -> void:
+		custom_minimum_size = Vector2(212, 132)
+		focus_mode = Control.FOCUS_NONE
+		UI.light_button(self)
+		toggle_mode = true
+
+	func _ready() -> void:
+		set_pressed_no_signal(picked)
+
+	func _draw() -> void:
+		var lit := button_pressed   # (the piece in hand: dark ink on the lit tile)
+		var col := (NeonTheme.INK if lit else NeonTheme.HEAD) if ok else NeonTheme.DISABLED
+		BuildKit.draw_icon(self, id, Rect2(Vector2(size.x * 0.5 - 38, 6), Vector2(76, 70)), col)
+		var f := get_theme_default_font()
+		var name := str(BuildKit.info(id).get("name", id))
+		var fs := 16
+		var w := f.get_string_size(name, HORIZONTAL_ALIGNMENT_LEFT, -1, fs).x
+		draw_string(f, Vector2((size.x - w) * 0.5, 96), name, HORIZONTAL_ALIGNMENT_LEFT, -1, fs, (NeonTheme.INK if lit else NeonTheme.TEXT) if ok else NeonTheme.DISABLED)
+		var w2 := f.get_string_size(cost, HORIZONTAL_ALIGNMENT_LEFT, -1, 14).x
+		draw_string(f, Vector2((size.x - w2) * 0.5, 120), cost, HORIZONTAL_ALIGNMENT_LEFT, size.x - 8, 14, (NeonTheme.INK if lit else NeonTheme.TEXT_DIM) if ok else Color(1.0, 0.4, 0.3))
+
+
+## A paint's swatch.
+class Swatch:
+	extends Button
+	var paint := 0
+	var on := false
+
+	func _init() -> void:
+		custom_minimum_size = Vector2(40, 38)
+		focus_mode = Control.FOCUS_NONE
+		UI.light_button(self)
+
+	func _draw() -> void:
+		var r := Rect2(Vector2(6, 6), size - Vector2(12, 12))
+		if paint == 0:
+			draw_line(r.position, r.end, NeonTheme.TEXT_DIM, 2.0)
+			draw_rect(r, NeonTheme.TEXT_DIM, false, 1.5)
+		else:
+			draw_rect(r, BuildKit.PAINTS[paint])
+		if on:
+			draw_rect(Rect2(Vector2(2, 2), size - Vector2(4, 4)), NeonTheme.HEAD, false, 2.5)

hunks.note: A modal window made in code. The choices go straight into CosmosBuilds' settings, and clicking a piece puts it in hand and shuts the menu.

bubbles.text: The nine categories of the kit, one tab each.
Built the first time it opens: the header, the category tabs, a five-column grid of piece tiles, then the TIER, STYLE, PAINT and MODE rows of toggle buttons.
Every row's buttons call this one function, which sets the builder's tier, style, paint or mode (or flips snapping) and redraws the menu.
Opens on the category of the piece already in hand, with the hexagon reveal used by the game's other menus.
refresh rebuilds the grid for the chosen category: each tile shows its cost in the current tier, whether you can afford it, and whether it's the piece in hand.

bubbles.at: _note.text = "%s: floors reach %d cell%s past a wall or pillar
bubbles.text: A line says what the tier means in play: how far its floors reach past a support and how tough its walls are. The line under it shows how much timber, stone, marble and bronze you have.
A piece is affordable when you have every material it costs. Under free building everything is.
A piece's tile draws the kit's icon, its name and its cost. The cost turns red when you can't afford it, and the piece in hand is drawn in dark ink on a lit tile.

+	list.add_theme_constant_override("separation", 4)

+
+
+func open(pc: Dictionary) -> void:
+	if _root == null:
+		_build()
+	chest = pc
+	if not chest.has("inv"):
+		chest["inv"] = {}
+	var was_open := visible and not HexReveal.closing(self)
+	show()
+	refresh()
+	if not was_open:
+		HexReveal.play(self)
+
+
+func close() -> void:
+	if not visible:
+		return
+	HexReveal.play(self, true, hide)
+
+
+func refresh() -> void:
+	UI.clear(_mine)
+	UI.clear(_its)
+	var d: Node = CosmosGame.data
+	var mine := {}
+	for k in d.carried:
+		mine[k] = int(mine.get(k, 0)) + int(d.carried[k])
+	for k in d.items:
+		mine[k] = int(mine.get(k, 0)) + int(d.items[k])
+	var keys := mine.keys()
+	keys.sort()
+	for k in keys:
+		if int(mine[k]) > 0 and Items.exists(k) and not Inventory.is_tool_id(k):
+			_mine.add_child(_row(k, int(mine[k]), true))
+	var inv: Dictionary = chest["inv"]
+	var ck := inv.keys()
+	ck.sort()
+	for k in ck:
+		if int(inv[k]) > 0:
+			_its.add_child(_row(k, int(inv[k]), false))
+	if ck.is_empty():
+		_its.add_child(UI.label("Empty - up to %d stacks" % BuildKit.CHEST_SLOTS, 16, NeonTheme.TEXT_DIM))
+	UI.scale_fonts(_root, "menu", 1.3)
+
+
+func _row(id: String, n: int, mine: bool) -> HBoxContainer:
+	var h := HBoxContainer.new()
+	h.add_theme_constant_override("separation", 8)
+	var ic := TextureRect.new()
+	ic.texture = Items.icon_texture(id)
+	ic.custom_minimum_size = Vector2(32, 32)
+	ic.expand_mode = TextureRect.EXPAND_IGNORE_SIZE
+	ic.stretch_mode = TextureRect.STRETCH_KEEP_ASPECT_CENTERED
+	h.add_child(ic)
+	var l := UI.label("%s  x%d" % [Items.display_name(id), n], 16, NeonTheme.TEXT)
+	l.size_flags_horizontal = SIZE_EXPAND_FILL
+	h.add_child(l)
+	for amount in [1, n]:
+		var b := UI.light_button(UI.button(("Store " if mine else "Take ") + ("1" if amount == 1 and n > 1 else "all"), func(): move(id, amount, mine), 15))
+		b.focus_mode = Control.FOCUS_NONE
+		h.add_child(b)
+		if n == 1:
+			break
+	return h
+
+
+## Moves `n` of `id` into the chest (`store`) or out of it into your hold. How many went.
+func move(id: String, n: int, store: bool) -> int:
+	var d: Node = CosmosGame.data
+	var inv: Dictionary = chest["inv"]
+	for k in inv.keys():
+		inv[k] = int(inv[k])
+	var moved := 0
+	if store:
+		n = mini(n, Inventory.room_for(inv, id, BuildKit.CHEST_SLOTS))
+		var from_c := Inventory.take(d.carried, id, n)
+		moved = from_c
+		if moved < n:
+			var k := mini(n - moved, d.count(id))
+			if k > 0 and d.remove_item(id, k):
+				moved += k
+		if moved > 0:
+			inv[id] = int(inv.get(id, 0)) + moved
+	else:
+		n = mini(n, int(inv.get(id, 0)))
+		if n > 0:
+			Inventory.take(inv, id, n)
+			d.add_item(id, n)
+			moved = n
+	d.changed.emit()
+	refresh()
+	return moved
+
+
+func _input(event: InputEvent) -> void:
+	if not visible or UI.esc_menu_open():
+		return
+	if event.is_action_pressed("ui_cancel"):
+		close()
+		get_viewport().set_input_as_handled()

It now has your one inventory, the automaton's toolbar with a row of its tools, and the automaton's equipment drawn large. The ship's equipment screen, stats, weapons row, in-space toolbar and the separate on-foot pack are gone from it.

bubbles.text: The new header: one inventory, one toolbar, the automaton's equipment.
The equipment screen grows to all the room left, so the automaton is drawn as large as the page allows.
The automaton's five tools are shown as draggable slots (src "tool"), so you can put them back on the toolbar after clearing a slot.

An inventory slot takes stacks from the inventory itself (to arrange them) and gear dragged off the automaton.

bubbles.at: return "Drag it onto the toolbar, or hover it and press 1-9."
bubbles.text: The tooltip hint now says what the item can do: equip it, put it on the toolbar, or just arrange it.

files.explanation: The solar map is now MAP > SOLAR SYSTEM. It shows the worlds where they really are on their orbits (the game's own orbit code), always shows the world you're on, and opens centred on you. It's also fluid: everything that moves is placed again every screen frame, and the stems, feet and sensor ring are moved line meshes instead of being rebuilt.

+## The globe's mesh (a worker's): a cube-sphere, N x N quads a face, each
+## vertex on the ground (raised EXAG times), its colour the ground's (linear),
+## its normal from its neighbours (a ring past the face's edges: no seams).
+static func build_globe(shape: PlanetShape) -> ArrayMesh:
+	var verts := PackedVector3Array()
+	var norms := PackedVector3Array()
+	var cols := PackedColorArray()
+	var idx := PackedInt32Array()
+	var uvs := PackedVector2Array()
+	var wet := shape.sea == 1 or shape.sea == 3
+	var S := N + 3                 # (samples a side: the face's N + 1, and one more each way)
+	for f in 6:
+		var ax := PlanetShape.face_axes(f)
+		var pts := PackedVector3Array()
+		pts.resize(S * S)
+		var hs := PackedFloat32Array()
+		hs.resize(S * S)
+		for j in S:
+			for i in S:
+				var d := PlanetShape.face_dir(ax[0], ax[1], ax[2], -1.0 + 2.0 * (i - 1) / N, -1.0 + 2.0 * (j - 1) / N)
+				var h := 0.0 if shape.kind == "gas" else shape.height(d)
+				hs[j * S + i] = h
+				pts[j * S + i] = d * R * (1.0 + (maxf(h, 0.0) if shape.sea > 0 else h) / shape.radius * EXAG)
+		var base := verts.size()
+		for j in range(1, N + 2):
+			for i in range(1, N + 2):
+				var p := pts[j * S + i]
+				var n := (pts[j * S + i + 1] - pts[j * S + i - 1]).cross(pts[(j + 1) * S + i] - pts[(j - 1) * S + i]).normalized()
+				if n.dot(p) < 0.0:
+					n = -n
+				verts.append(p)
+				norms.append(n)
+				var h := hs[j * S + i]
+				cols.append(ground_colour(shape, p.normalized(), maxf(h, 0.0) if wet else h).srgb_to_linear())
+				uvs.append(Vector2(h / shape.amp, 0.0))   # (the seas coloured in the shader by it: smooth shores)
+		var W := N + 1
+		var flip := false
+		var p0 := verts[base]
+		if (verts[base + 1] - p0).cross(verts[base + W] - p0).dot(p0) > 0.0:
+			flip = true   # (Godot's front faces wind clockwise)
+		for j in N:
+			for i in N:
+				var a := base + j * W + i
+				if flip:
+					idx.append_array([a, a + W, a + 1, a + 1, a + W, a + W + 1])
+				else:
+					idx.append_array([a, a + 1, a + W, a + 1, a + W + 1, a + W])
+	var arr := []
+	arr.resize(Mesh.ARRAY_MAX)
+	arr[Mesh.ARRAY_VERTEX] = verts
+	arr[Mesh.ARRAY_NORMAL] = norms
+	arr[Mesh.ARRAY_COLOR] = cols
+	arr[Mesh.ARRAY_TEX_UV] = uvs
+	arr[Mesh.ARRAY_INDEX] = idx
+	var m := ArrayMesh.new()
+	m.add_surface_from_arrays(Mesh.PRIMITIVE_TRIANGLES, arr)
+	return m

+			elif absf(_dist_t - _set_dist) > _set_dist * 1e-6:
+				_update_ground()
+				_span_t = _span_of_dist(_dist_t)
+				_anim = {}
+			_update_ground()
+			if not _anim.is_empty():
+				_anim["t"] += delta
+				var u := clampf(_anim["t"] / _anim["dur"], 0.0, 1.0)
+				# (linear in the zoom - px a metre: quick down to the town, slow as its plan comes in)
+				span = 1.0 / lerpf(1.0 / _anim["s0"], 1.0 / _anim["s1"], smoothstep(0.0, 1.0, u))
+				_span_t = span
+				if _anim["turn"]:
+					var ua := smoothstep(0.0, 0.65, u)   # (turned to it first, then down onto it)
+					yaw = lerpf(_anim["y0"], _anim["y1"], ua)
+					_yaw_t = yaw
+					pitch = lerpf(_anim["p0"], _anim["p1"], ua)
+					_pitch_t = pitch
+				mark_dirty()
+				if u >= 1.0:
+					_anim = {}
+			else:
+				_span_t = clampf(_span_t, span_min(), span_max())
+				if absf(log(span / _span_t)) > 0.0005:
+					span = exp(lerpf(log(span), log(_span_t), 1.0 - exp(-delta * 10.0)))
+					mark_dirty()
+				elif span != _span_t:
+					span = _span_t
+					mark_dirty()
+			_apply_span()
+		super._process(delta)
+		if not is_visible_in_tree() or _sh == null:
+			return
+		# All the way in over a town you've been in: its plan alone.
+		if town != "" and _anim.is_empty() and blend > 0.999 and span <= span_min() * 1.0005 and _span_t <= span_min() * 1.0005:
+			page._to_plan()
+
+	## The wheel: nearer or farther; coming in, it turns toward the town
+	## you've been in that it's over (else a little toward the cursor).
+	func zoom(f: float, at := Vector2(-1, -1)) -> void:
+		if _sh == null:
+			return
+		_anim = {}
+		var lo := span_min()
+		var want := _span_t * f
+		if f < 1.0 and town != "" and want < lo:
+			_carry = minf(_carry * lo / want, 20.0)
+		elif f > 1.0:
+			_carry = 1.0
+		_span_t = clampf(want, lo, span_max())
+		if f >= 1.0:
+			return
+		if town != "":
+			var u: Vector3 = _town_dir(town)[0]
+			var k := clampf((1.0 - f) * 2.5, 0.0, 1.0)
+			_pitch_t = lerpf(_pitch_t, -asin(clampf(u.y, -1.0, 1.0)), k)
+			_yaw_t = _yaw_t + wrapf(atan2(u.x, u.z) - _yaw_t, -PI, PI) * k
+		elif at.x >= 0.0:
+			var o := cam.project_ray_origin(at)
+			var dir := cam.project_ray_normal(at)
+			var b := o.dot(dir)
+			var disc := b * b - (o.length_squared() - R * R)
+			if disc > 0.0:
+				var hit := o + dir * (-b - sqrt(disc))
+				var u := hit.normalized()
+				var k := (1.0 - f) * 1.2
+				_pitch_t = lerpf(_pitch_t, -asin(clampf(u.y, -1.0, 1.0)), k)
+				_yaw_t = _yaw_t + wrapf(atan2(u.x, u.z) - _yaw_t, -PI, PI) * k
+
+	## The keys and the pad: their zoom through zoom(), their turn as slow as the view's near.
+	func _controls(delta: float) -> void:
+		var d0 := _dist_t
+		var y0 := _yaw_t
+		var p0 := _pitch_t
+		var mn := min_dist
+		min_dist = 1e-4
+		super._controls(delta)
+		min_dist = mn
+		if _dist_t != d0:
+			var f := _dist_t / d0
+			_dist_t = d0
+			zoom(f)
+		if _yaw_t != y0 or _pitch_t != p0:
+			_anim = {}
+			var k := clampf(span / _tan() / (R * 1.6), 0.0002, 1.0)
+			_yaw_t = y0 + (_yaw_t - y0) * k
+			_pitch_t = p0 + (_pitch_t - p0) * k
+
+	## (A double click flies to a mark: the globe turns to it - it never leaves the middle.)
+	func fly_to(at: Vector3, d := -1.0) -> void:
+		if at == Vector3.ZERO:
+			super.fly_to(at, d)
+		else:
+			turn_to(at, d)
+
+	func fit(now := false) -> void:
+		if now:
+			snap_to(Vector3.ZERO, R * 2.7)
+		else:
+			fly_to(Vector3.ZERO, R * 2.7)
+
+	## Turns the globe to put `d` (planet-local) before you; `d_to`: how near.
+	func turn_to(d: Vector3, d_to := -1.0) -> void:
+		var u := d.normalized()
+		_anim = {}
+		_pitch_t = -asin(clampf(u.y, -1.0, 1.0))
+		_yaw_t = yaw + wrapf(atan2(u.x, u.z) - yaw, -PI, PI)
+		_focus_t = Vector3.ZERO
+		if d_to > 0.0:
+			_dist_t = clampf(d_to, min_dist, max_dist)
+
+	func centre_on_you() -> void:
+		var o: Dictionary = all.get("you", all.get("ship", {}))
+		if not o.is_empty():
+			turn_to(o["dir"], R * 1.6)
+
+	func look_at_selected() -> void:
+		if all.has(selected_key):
+			turn_to(all[selected_key]["dir"], minf(_dist_t, R * 1.5))
+
+	func cycle_order() -> Array:
+		return marks.keys()
+
+	func cycle(d := 1) -> void:
+		var keys := cycle_order()
+		if keys.is_empty():
+			return
+		var i := keys.find(selected_key)
+		var k: String = keys[wrapi(i + d, 0, keys.size())] if i >= 0 else keys[0]
+		select(k)
+		turn_to(all[k]["dir"])
+
+	func clicked(key: String, _add: bool) -> void:
+		if key == "":
+			return
+		select(key)
+		var o: Dictionary = all[key]
+		if o["kind"] == "town" and o["visited"]:
+			page.open_plan(key)
+
+	func accept() -> void:
+		if all.has(selected_key):
+			page.open_plan(selected_key)
+
+	## Dragging turns it (as if you held the ground, near) - no panning off it.
+	func pan(rel: Vector2) -> void:
+		_turn(rel)
+
+	func _turn(rel: Vector2) -> void:
+		_anim = {}
+		var k := clampf(span / _tan() / (R * 1.6), 0.0, 1.0)
+		var grab := 2.0 * span / maxf(size.y, 8.0) / _ground   # (rad a px: the ground under the cursor follows it)
+		_yaw_t -= rel.x * maxf(0.008 * k, grab / maxf(cos(_pitch_t), 0.2))
+		_pitch_t = clampf(_pitch_t - rel.y * maxf(0.006 * k, grab), -1.5, 1.5)
+
+	func _gui_input(ev: InputEvent) -> void:
+		if ev is InputEventMouseMotion and _drag != "":
+			var mm := ev as InputEventMouseMotion
+			if mm.position.distance_to(_press) > 4.0 or _moved:
+				_moved = true
+				_turn(mm.relative)
+				accept_event()
+				return
+		super._gui_input(ev)
+
+	## The picture and the marks over it - near the ground, the marks where
+	## they stand on it (as the town's plan has them).
+	func _draw() -> void:
+		draw_texture_rect(vp.get_texture(), Rect2(Vector2.ZERO, size), false)
+		_screen = {}
+		_behind = {}
+		var w := clampf(1.0 - span / span_floor(), 0.0, 1.0)
+		for key in marks:
+			var p: Vector3 = marks[key]["pos"]
+			if w > 0.0 and marks[key].has("ground"):
+				p = p.lerp(marks[key]["ground"], w)
+			if cam.is_position_behind(p):
+				_behind[key] = true
+				continue
+			_screen[key] = cam.unproject_position(p)
+		draw_overlay()
+
+	func draw_overlay() -> void:
+		var font := NeonTheme.heavy_font()
+		var fa := 1.0 - smoothstep(0.35, 0.85, blend)   # (the marks giving way to the plan's)
+		if _sh != null and not _globe.visible:
+			draw_string(font, size * 0.5 - Vector2(80, 0), "Charting the world...", HORIZONTAL_ALIGNMENT_LEFT, -1, 18, NeonTheme.HEAD)
+		var taken: Array = []
+		var near := dist < R * 1.6
+		var order: Array = marks.keys()
+		order.sort_custom(func(a, b): return _rank(a) > _rank(b))
+		if fa <= 0.01:
+			return
+		for k in order:
+			var o: Dictionary = marks[k]
+			var p: Variant = at_screen(k)
+			if p == null:
+				continue
+			var sp: Vector2 = p
+			var col: Color = o["color"]
+			col.a *= fa
+			var white := Color(1, 1, 1, fa)
+			var hot: bool = k == selected_key or k == hover_key
+			match str(o["kind"]):
+				"town":
+					var rr := 7.0 if o["city"] else 5.0
+					draw_rect(Rect2(sp - Vector2(rr, rr), Vector2(rr, rr) * 2.0), Color(col, 0.95), false, 2.0)
+					if o["city"]:
+						draw_line(sp + Vector2(-rr, -rr - 4), sp + Vector2(rr, -rr - 4), col, 2.0)
+					if o["visited"]:
+						draw_rect(Rect2(sp - Vector2(2, 2), Vector2(4, 4)), col)
+				"cave", "dungeon":
+					draw_arc(sp, 6.0, PI, TAU, 10, col, 2.0)
+					draw_line(sp + Vector2(-6, 0), sp + Vector2(6, 0), col, 2.0)
+				"camp":
+					draw_line(sp + Vector2(-5, -5), sp + Vector2(5, 5), col, 2.0)
+					draw_line(sp + Vector2(-5, 5), sp + Vector2(5, -5), col, 2.0)
+				"ship":
+					draw_colored_polygon(PackedVector2Array([sp + Vector2(0, -9), sp + Vector2(7, 7), sp + Vector2(-7, 7)]), col)
+				"you":
+					draw_circle(sp, 6.0, white)
+					# (your heading: along the ground, as the globe shows it)
+					var d: Vector3 = o["dir"]
+					var hd: float = o["heading"]
+					var f3: Vector3 = (o["north"] as Vector3) * cos(hd) + (o["east"] as Vector3) * sin(hd)
+					var ahead: Variant = project((o["pos"] as Vector3) + f3 * R * 0.03)
+					if ahead != null and (ahead as Vector2).distance_to(sp) > 0.5:
+						draw_line(sp, sp + ((ahead as Vector2) - sp).normalized() * 16.0, white, 2.0)
+			if hot:
+				_brackets(sp, 12.0, col)
+			if k == selected_key or k == hover_key or o["kind"] in ["town", "you", "ship"] or near:
+				if fa >= 0.99:
+					tag(sp + Vector2(0, -12), str(o["name"]), 15, col, taken, font)
+				else:
+					_fading_tag(sp + Vector2(0, -12), str(o["name"]), col, taken, font, fa)
+
+	## A name tag (as tag()) fading out, its outline with it: the plan's names coming in instead.
+	func _fading_tag(at: Vector2, text: String, col: Color, taken: Array, font: Font, a: float) -> void:
+		var w := font.get_string_size(text, HORIZONTAL_ALIGNMENT_LEFT, -1, 15).x
+		var r := Rect2(at - Vector2(w * 0.5, 15), Vector2(w, 18))
+		var pad := r.grow_individual(8.0, 2.0, 8.0, 2.0)
+		for q: Rect2 in taken:
+			if q.intersects(pad):
+				return
+		taken.append(r)
+		draw_string_outline(font, r.position + Vector2(0, 15), text, HORIZONTAL_ALIGNMENT_LEFT, -1, 15, 4, Color(0, 0, 0, 0.85 * a))
+		draw_string(font, r.position + Vector2(0, 15), text, HORIZONTAL_ALIGNMENT_LEFT, -1, 15, col)
+
+	func _rank(k: String) -> int:
+		if k == selected_key:
+			return 9
+		return {"you": 5, "ship": 4, "town": 3, "dungeon": 2, "cave": 2, "camp": 1}.get(all[k]["kind"], 0)
+
+	func _brackets(p: Vector2, r: float, col: Color) -> void:
+		for sx in [-1.0, 1.0]:
+			for sy in [-1.0, 1.0]:
+				var c := p + Vector2(sx, sy) * r
+				draw_line(c, c - Vector2(sx * 5.0, 0), col, 2.0)
+				draw_line(c, c - Vector2(0, sy * 5.0), col, 2.0)
+

+# --- A town's plan ---------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+## A town from above (its plan - bake_plan's picture), north up: its places
+## named, you on it. Coming in on the globe it's laid over it where the town
+## is (follow_globe: the globe's north and scale), `alpha` of it - its labels
+## coming last; all in (`full`), it's its own: the wheel zooms (eased, as the
+## globe's), dragging pans, a middle click fits it; zoomed out past the whole
+## town, back to the globe (PlanetMapPage.plan_out) the same way.
+class TownPlan extends Control:
+	var page: Node
+	var o := {}                  # the town's mark (PlanetMapPage.gather)
+	var key := ""                # (its plan's - PlanetMapPage._plans)
+	var t := {}                  # the planet (target())
+	var full := false            # (the plan alone: the globe zoomed all the way in)
+	var alpha := 1.0             # (how much of it shows over the globe)
+	var _frame := Transform3D.IDENTITY
+	var _rot := 0.0              # (the plan turned: north up)
+	var _north := 0.0            # (its turn north up, at the town)
+	var _ppm := 2.0              # zoom: px a metre (eased to _ppm_t)
+	var _ppm_t := 2.0
+	var _centre := Vector2.ZERO  # the middle of the view (town-local x, z)
+	var _anchor := Vector2.ZERO  # (the zoom's: the screen point kept on the same ground)
+	var _anchor_w := Vector2.ZERO
+	var _drag := false
+	var _rect := Rect2()
+
+	func _init() -> void:
+		mouse_filter = MOUSE_FILTER_STOP
+		clip_contents = true
+		texture_filter = TEXTURE_FILTER_LINEAR_WITH_MIPMAPS
+
+	func show_town(mark: Dictionary, k: String, planet_t: Dictionary) -> void:
+		o = mark
+		key = k
+		t = planet_t
+		var s: Dictionary = o["site"]
+		_frame = CosmosTown.frame(s, float(t["radius"]))
+		var n := _frame.basis.inverse() * Vector3.UP   # (north, in the town's own frame)
+		var n2 := Vector2(n.x, n.z)
+		_north = -PI * 0.5 - n2.angle() if n2.length() > 0.01 else 0.0
+		_rot = _north
+		_rect = PlanetMapPage.plan_rect(str(s["kind"]))
+		_centre = _rect.get_center()
+		_ppm = fit_ppm()
+		_ppm_t = _ppm
+
+	## The zoom showing the whole town (north up).
+	func fit_ppm() -> float:
+		var sz: Vector2 = size if size.x > 10.0 else (page._view.size if page and page._view.size.x > 10.0 else Vector2(880, 590))
+		var c := absf(cos(_north))
+		var sn := absf(sin(_north))
+		var w := maxf(_rect.size.x * c + _rect.size.y * sn, 1.0)   # (its box, turned north up)
+		var h := maxf(_rect.size.x * sn + _rect.size.y * c, 1.0)
+		return minf((sz.x - 40.0) / w, (sz.y - 70.0) / h)
+
+	## The whole town in view (eased).
+	func fit() -> void:
+		_anchor = size * 0.5
+		_anchor_w = _rect.get_center()
+		_ppm_t = fit_ppm()
+		_centre = _anchor_w
+		queue_redraw()
+
+	## Laid over the globe `v` as it shows the town now: under its middle, its
+	## north, its scale; `a` of it shown.
+	func follow_globe(v: Node, a: float) -> void:
+		full = false
+		alpha = a
+		mouse_filter = MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE
+		var up := _frame.basis.inverse() * (v.cam.transform.basis.y as Vector3)
+		_rot = -PI * 0.5 - Vector2(up.x, up.z).angle() if Vector2(up.x, up.z).length() > 0.01 else _north
+		var g := _frame.affine_inverse() * ((v.view_dir() as Vector3) * _frame.origin.length())
+		_centre = Vector2(g.x, g.z)
+		_ppm = v.ppm()
+		_ppm_t = _ppm
+		queue_redraw()
+
+	## All in: the plan alone from here, at `p` px a metre (the wheel's zoom past it: `carry`).
+	func enter(p: float, carry: float) -> void:
+		full = true
+		alpha = 1.0
+		mouse_filter = MOUSE_FILTER_STOP
+		_ppm = p
+		_ppm_t = clampf(p * carry, p, 24.0)
+		_anchor = size * 0.5
+		_anchor_w = _centre
+		queue_redraw()
+
+	## The middle of the view, as a direction (planet-local).
+	func centre_dir() -> Vector3:
+		return (_frame * Vector3(_centre.x, 0.0, _centre.y)).normalized()
+
+	func _process(delta: float) -> void:
+		if not is_visible_in_tree():
+			return
+		if full and absf(log(_ppm / _ppm_t)) > 1e-4:
+			_ppm = exp(lerpf(log(_ppm), log(_ppm_t), 1.0 - exp(-delta * 10.0)))
+			if absf(log(_ppm / _ppm_t)) <= 1e-4:
+				_ppm = _ppm_t
+			_centre = _anchor_w - (_anchor - size * 0.5).rotated(-_rot) / _ppm
+			queue_redraw()
+		elif UI.redraw_due(self, 6.0):
+			queue_redraw()
+
+	## Town-local (x, z) -> the screen.
+	func to_screen(p: Vector2) -> Vector2:
+		return size * 0.5 + ((p - _centre) * _ppm).rotated(_rot)
+
+	func from_screen(s: Vector2) -> Vector2:
+		return ((s - size * 0.5).rotated(-_rot) / _ppm) + _centre
+
+	func _draw() -> void:
+		var a := 1.0 if full else alpha
+		var bg := 1.0 if full else smoothstep(0.5, 1.0, a)   # (the globe round the town goes last)
+		if bg > 0.0:
+			draw_rect(Rect2(Vector2.ZERO, size), Color(0.02, 0.02, 0.03, bg))
+		var font := NeonTheme.heavy_font()
+		var tex := PlanetMapPage.plan_texture(key)
+		if tex == null:
+			if full:
+				draw_string(font, size * 0.5 - Vector2(90, 0), "Drawing the town's plan...", HORIZONTAL_ALIGNMENT_LEFT, -1, 18, NeonTheme.HEAD)
+			return
+		draw_set_transform(to_screen(_rect.position), _rot, Vector2.ONE * _ppm / PlanetMapPage.PLAN_PPM)
+		draw_texture(tex, Vector2.ZERO, Color(1, 1, 1, a))
+		draw_set_transform(Vector2.ZERO)
+		var s: Dictionary = o["site"]
+		# The places, named (they come in after the buildings).
+		var taken: Array = []
+		var la := 1.0 if full else smoothstep(0.3, 0.8, a)
+		if la > 0.01:
+			var fs := 15 if _ppm < 4.0 else 17
+			for p in CosmosTown.places(str(s["kind"])):
+				var at := to_screen(Vector2((p[2] as Vector3).x, (p[2] as Vector3).z))
+				var people: bool = p[0] in ["vendor", "courier", "pilot"]
+				var col := Color(NeonTheme.INFO if people else NeonTheme.HEAD, la)
+				if people:
+					draw_circle(at, 5.0, col)
+				else:
+					draw_rect(Rect2(at - Vector2(5, 5), Vector2(10, 10)), col, false, 2.0)
+				_label(at + Vector2(9, 5), str(p[1]), fs, col, taken, font)
+		# You, and your ship (the globe's marks give way to these).
+		var ya := 1.0 if full else smoothstep(0.35, 0.85, a)
+		var c: Node = page.cosmos()
+		var node: Node3D = t.get("node")
+		if c and node and ya > 0.01:
+			var info := Color(NeonTheme.INFO, ya)
+			var white := Color(1, 1, 1, ya)
+			if c.ship and is_instance_valid(c.ship):
+				var sp3: Vector3 = _frame.affine_inverse() * (c.ship.global_position - node.global_position)
+				if absf(sp3.y) < 400.0:
+					var sp := to_screen(Vector2(sp3.x, sp3.z))
+					draw_colored_polygon(PackedVector2Array([sp + Vector2(0, -9), sp + Vector2(7, 7), sp + Vector2(-7, 7)]), info)
+					_label(sp + Vector2(10, 5), "Your ship", 15, info, taken, font)
+			if c.walker and c.walker.planet == node:
+				var wl: Vector3 = _frame.affine_inverse() * (c.walker.global_position - node.global_position)
+				var wp := to_screen(Vector2(wl.x, wl.z))
+				var f: Vector3 = _frame.basis.inverse() * (c.walker.facing as Vector3)
+				var dir := Vector2(f.x, f.z).normalized().rotated(_rot)
+				draw_circle(wp, 6.0, white)
+				draw_line(wp, wp + dir * 16.0, white, 2.0)
+				_label(wp + Vector2(10, 5), "You", 15, white, taken, font)
+		# The town's name, north, the scale.
+		var ta := 1.0 if full else smoothstep(0.7, 1.0, a)
+		if ta <= 0.01:
+			return
+		var head := Color(NeonTheme.HEAD, ta)
+		var text := Color(NeonTheme.TEXT, ta)
+		var title := str(o["town"]).to_upper() + ("  -  CITY" if o["city"] else "  -  VILLAGE")
+		draw_string_outline(font, Vector2(16, 30), title, HORIZONTAL_ALIGNMENT_LEFT, -1, 22, 4, Color(0, 0, 0, 0.85 * ta))
+		draw_string(font, Vector2(16, 30), title, HORIZONTAL_ALIGNMENT_LEFT, -1, 22, head)
+		var nc := Vector2(size.x - 34, 40)
+		var nd := Vector2.UP.rotated(_rot - _north)   # (north: up, unless the globe's turned it a little)
+		draw_colored_polygon(PackedVector2Array([nc + nd * 16.0, nc + nd.rotated(2.5) * 9.0, nc + nd.rotated(-2.5) * 9.0]), head)
+		draw_string(font, nc + Vector2(-6, 26), "N", HORIZONTAL_ALIGNMENT_LEFT, -1, 16, head)
+		var m := 50.0 if _ppm < 3.0 else (20.0 if _ppm < 8.0 else 10.0)
+		if _ppm < 1.0:
+			m = 100.0 if _ppm > 0.5 else 200.0
+		var b0 := Vector2(16, size.y - 20)
+		draw_line(b0, b0 + Vector2(m * _ppm, 0), text, 2.0)

+		var w := font.get_string_size(text, HORIZONTAL_ALIGNMENT_LEFT, -1, fs).x
+		var r := Rect2(at - Vector2(0, fs), Vector2(w, fs * 1.2))
+		for q: Rect2 in taken:
+			if q.intersects(r):
+				r.position.y += fs * 1.25   # (one under the other)

+	func zoom(f: float, at := Vector2(-1, -1)) -> void:

+		_anchor = at if at.x >= 0.0 else size * 0.5
+		_anchor_w = from_screen(_anchor)
+		var want := _ppm_t * f
+		if f < 1.0 and want < fit_ppm() * 0.999:
+			page.plan_out(_ppm, want)

+		_ppm_t = minf(want, 24.0)
+
+	func _gui_input(ev: InputEvent) -> void:
+		if not full:
+			return
+		if ev is InputEventMouseButton:
+			var mb := ev as InputEventMouseButton
+			if mb.pressed and mb.button_index == MOUSE_BUTTON_WHEEL_UP:
+				zoom(1.0 / 0.85, mb.position)
+			elif mb.pressed and mb.button_index == MOUSE_BUTTON_WHEEL_DOWN:
+				zoom(0.85, mb.position)

+			elif mb.button_index in [MOUSE_BUTTON_LEFT, MOUSE_BUTTON_RIGHT]:

+			accept_event()
+		elif ev is InputEventMouseMotion and _drag:

+			_anchor_w = from_screen(_anchor)
+			queue_redraw()
+			accept_event()
+
+	func _input(ev: InputEvent) -> void:
+		if not full or not is_visible_in_tree() or UI.esc_menu_open():

+		if ev is InputEventKey and ev.pressed and not ev.echo:

hunks.title: The globe, the fog, the marks and the town plans
hunks.note: A worker builds the globe mesh from PlanetShape, and the fog hides ground you haven't seen. Marks are gathered only where explored. GlobeView zooms by span and hands over to TownPlan as you come close to a visited town.

bubbles.text: A cube-sphere: each vertex is on the real ground (raised EXAG times) and coloured from the planet's palette. Normals come from neighbouring samples, including a ring past each face's edge, so the faces meet without seams. The UV carries the height so the shader can colour the seas with smooth shores.
Towns show once explored or visited; caves, dungeons and pirate camps only in explored ground; your ship while it's within three radii; and you with your heading.

How much of the plan shows, from how many pixels a metre the globe is at the town. It's eased on a log scale, from none at a third of the plan's own zoom to all of it at that zoom, so it fades in over about seven wheel notches.

bubbles.at: static func bake_plan(kind: String, seed: int, empire: String) -> Image:
bubbles.text: Drawn on a worker from the town's own solids (CosmosTown.plan_of): the square and the landing field, then the buildings lowest first, lighter the taller, each edged dark. It's mipmapped so it stays smooth while small on screen.
The zoom is one value, span (half the view's height on the ground). The camera comes down to 3% of the radius over the ground and then narrows its field of view instead of going lower.
Finds the visited town the middle of the view is over, and keeps it while you're close or a dive is under way, so the plan doesn't flicker on and off at the edge.

bubbles.at: func fly_into(key: String, secs: float) -> void:
bubbles.text: A click on a town, or Town plan: an eased 0.7 s dive that turns to the town first and then zooms down. The zoom is eased in pixels a metre, so it's quick at first and slows as the plan comes in.

bubbles.at: func follow_globe(v: Node, a: float) -> void:
bubbles.text: While blending in, the plan is laid exactly where the town is: under the view's middle, turned to the globe camera's north, and at the globe's pixels a metre.
Fully zoomed in over the town: the plan takes over on its own, with any spare wheel zoom carried on. Zooming out past it hands back to the globe the same way (plan_out, take_over).

-## your automaton's parts (Parts), opened up one at a time on the operating
-## table and repaired by hand, like surgery:
-##   - the schematic and the part list on the left: how well each part works,
-##     the faults found in it and the "?" of damage not yet traced;
-##   - the table: the part's casing (bolts to undo - opposite ones, never
-##     neighbours, or the casing warps and cracks), then its components, the
-##     cables between them and the faults the scanner has found;
-##   - the right: the vitals (temperature, pressure, power, a pulse that

-## Tools: the scanner (a lens swept over the part: faults of its mode show,

-## The automaton is operated on as a body (Surgery): the table shows its
